title: PR detail stays stale after status refresh and agent actions
impact: Users cannot trust the displayed checks, comments, description, or generated guide to reflect the current PR. A running check can remain running after completion.
recommendation: Give detail a refresh command and invalidation keyed by repository, PR and head/revision. Refresh activity after writes and checks while pending. Preserve a timestamp and stale state.
acceptance: Open a PR with a pending check, finish the check remotely, add a comment, and invoke Refresh PR status. The same panel shows the new result and comment. A new guide appears after its agent completes without reopening the PR.

title: Reload discards the last good PR and replaces it with a transient error
impact: A temporary network or authentication failure removes previously readable review context, including access to the Code tab body.
recommendation: Store last-success, pending and error separately. Preserve content on retriable failures and clear it only when authoritative identity or absence changes.
acceptance: Load a PR, simulate a failed refresh, and verify that title, discussion and diff remain visible with an actionable stale/error indicator. Retry succeeds without closing the tab.

title: Authentication and retry guidance do not form a working recovery flow
impact: Users see no PR or a dead-end instruction instead of a recoverable authentication error. Missing CLI, expired credentials and a branch with no PR look identical during discovery.
recommendation: Propagate typed discovery failures to the PR opener and panel. Add a retry button bound to detail reload and make the displayed shortcut match the real binding. Keep host-specific login commands.
acceptance: With a mocked missing executable and then an expired login, show distinct remedies. After restoring authentication, clicking Retry must load the PR. The documented keyboard action must do the same.

title: Rewrite guide displays the oldest matching guide
impact: A rewritten guide can appear not to have changed, and reviewers can read superseded instructions.
recommendation: Select the newest by timestamp or honor the canonical newest-first contract. Add a fixture with multiple guides in real backend order.
acceptance: With older and newer guide comments from a human account, Guide displays the newer one. Rewriting and refreshing must replace it with the latest text.

title: Timeline reverses the backend order and has no ordering control
impact: New activity appears at the bottom of a long discussion despite the panel documenting newest-first behavior.
recommendation: Remove the accidental reversal or define a shared order contract and add a user preference.
acceptance: With comments at 09:00 and 10:00, the default Timeline begins with 10:00. Any oldest-first option visibly changes the order.

title: Timeline drops review replies, resolution state and quoted code
impact: Reviewers cannot see answers or distinguish open findings from already resolved or outdated discussions. A finding loses the code context needed to evaluate it.
recommendation: Render complete review threads and their state. Reuse the canonical thread model for Summary, Timeline and inline code comments.
acceptance: A fixture with a resolved, outdated thread and two replies exposes all four facts. The user can open the associated code location and distinguish it from an unresolved thread.

title: Capped PR data is presented as a complete conversation and check result
impact: A reviewer can mistake a partial list for all findings or all checks. Missing failure data can make the summary appear more reassuring than the complete PR.
recommendation: Show explicit partial-data notices separately for checks and discussion. Page remaining data where supported and withhold a complete-pass claim until coverage is known.
acceptance: Inject checks_truncated and comments_truncated independently. Each produces its own notice and route to more data. A truncated success-only subset never claims all checks pass.

title: Checks stop at names and icons without a route to failure details
impact: A failed job requires manually finding the run on the forge. Users cannot inspect the result from the displayed check or distinguish some important status categories.
recommendation: Carry check URLs and useful status distinctions through the model. Add a Details action with visible open failure handling.
acceptance: A failed job opens its own run page from the PR panel. Cancelled and approval-required runs have distinct labels and appropriate next actions.

title: Descriptions, comments and guides render as raw text
impact: PR templates, code fences, tables, checklists, image evidence and linked documents lose their intended presentation and interaction.
recommendation: Use a shared Markdown component with forge-relative links, image handling, code copy and safe task-list interaction.
acceptance: An example PR with a linked issue, fenced code, table, checklist and image renders each correctly. Links open their actual destinations and long code remains usable.

title: No native comment, reply, review verdict or resolution workflow
impact: Users must leave the PR pane or ask an agent to conduct the review. They cannot prepare a batch of inline comments and submit an approval or request changes in the UI.
recommendation: Add typed, permission-aware native review operations or explicitly label the limited workflow and provide reliable forge handoff. Keep failed review drafts.
acceptance: Compose an inline comment and approval, fail the submit once, retry without losing text, then see the posted review. Reply and resolve a thread and verify the new state after refresh.

title: PR metadata cannot be edited or managed in the native panel
impact: Users cannot correct a title or description, request reviewers, or apply labels while reviewing in Ferrite.
recommendation: Extend the domain model and add focused editors with explicit saving/error states and permission checks.
acceptance: Edit title/body and change labels/review requests without leaving the panel. A rejected save retains the draft and shows the reason.

title: Agent-backed PR operations have no panel-level pending, success or failure lifecycle
impact: Clicking Merge, Ready, Write guide or Create PR can appear to do nothing while work queues behind another turn. Repeated clicks can enqueue repeated requests.
recommendation: Keep agent execution if desired, but model an operation with a target, state and result. Show that state beside the initiating control and deduplicate repeated requests.
acceptance: Click an action while a turn is busy. Show Queued and the target PR, block duplicate enqueue, then transition through Running to success/failure and refresh the affected data.

title: Lifecycle actions lack inverse operations and branch maintenance
impact: A user can enable auto-merge or close a PR but cannot undo those choices from the same UI. Updating a stale branch and approving blocked workflows also require leaving the panel.
recommendation: Model the current settings and complete reversible lifecycle actions. Gate them by actual host capability and permission.
acceptance: Enable then disable auto-merge, close then reopen a PR, toggle maintainer edits both ways, and update an eligible branch. Each result appears after refresh.

title: PR action prompts lose canonical host and repository identity
impact: For forks, multiple remotes, enterprise hosts or non-GitHub forges, the agent must reconstruct the target and may fail or act in the wrong repository. No wrong-target mutation was performed in this audit.
recommendation: Carry an explicit target identity through every operation. For agent handoffs, include the URL and provider-specific command plus a target-verification step. Resolve branch deletion from the PR head repository.
acceptance: With origin=fork and upstream=base, generated operations target the named PR and correct remote branch. GitLab/Azure reads generate matching provider operations or clearly unavailable controls.

title: Concurrent PR reads can land out of order and retire the current tab
impact: A slow old response can overwrite newer details, or remove the tab for the PR now on the branch. The source permits this race; timing was not reproduced.
recommendation: Capture canonical target and request generation, deduplicate pending reads, and reject stale completions before they modify cache or surfaces.
acceptance: Delay read A, start read B for a different current PR, complete B then A. B stays visible and its tab remains. Repeated open of one pending PR creates one request.

title: PR read workers have no effective cancellation or deadline
impact: A hung forge process can leave Reading visible indefinitely and retain a worker after the pane is closed. Repeated forced opens can accumulate stuck reads.
recommendation: Thread cancellation and a deadline through the one-shot adapter; cancel on supersession and release the process tree. Share equivalent safeguards with badge discovery.
acceptance: A fake gh that never exits reaches a visible timeout. Closing or superseding the request terminates its process tree, and repeated retries do not leave worker processes behind.

title: Review verdicts and empty-body approvals are absent from the snapshot
impact: Reviewers cannot tell who approved, requested changes, or had a review dismissed. An approval with no written body disappears entirely.
recommendation: Preserve structured review outcomes, including empty-body verdicts and whether the review applies to the latest head.
acceptance: An approval with an empty body appears with author and verdict. A later push marks an old review appropriately. Changes requested and dismissed reviews remain distinguishable.

title: PR panel omits the checkout-versus-host sync warning
impact: Users may confuse local changes shown in Code with what reviewers can actually see on the host, because the PR view drops the unpushed/behind warning.
recommendation: Restore the sync notice and explicitly identify which revision Code displays. Prefer the hosted PR revisions for hosted review operations.
acceptance: With two unpushed commits, the PR panel says so and identifies the displayed code revision. With a behind checkout, it does not silently present the local diff as the current hosted PR.

title: Guide is a comment convention without revision-aware review workflow
impact: A guide can remain apparently current after a push, and its file references cannot act as a structured review tour. Guide generation has no local run or failure state.
recommendation: Decide whether a comment guide is an intentional reduced feature. At minimum record head identity, generation state and stale status. Full parity needs ordered stops with linked excerpts.
acceptance: After generating a guide, push a new commit. The guide is visibly stale. A failed rewrite retains the old guide and offers retry; successful stops open the corresponding file and lines.

title: Create PR is unavailable for branch work absent from the current thread transcript
impact: A user who opens a prepared branch, makes manual edits, or imports work from another session cannot use the native Create PR button unless this thread has recorded file edits.
recommendation: Offer Create PR from repository state or a stable command, independent of transcript-derived change cards. Preserve the current agent handoff if that is the chosen creation design.
acceptance: Open a fresh thread on a branch with an ahead-of-base commit created outside Ferrite. Create PR is discoverable and targets that branch. No synthetic agent edit is required.

title: Merge controls ignore permissions, allowed methods and readiness
impact: The panel offers actions the user cannot perform and always presents Merge on an open PR, even with conflicts or blocked checks. The user cannot choose a supported merge method.
recommendation: Fetch viewer permissions, available merge methods and readiness. Disable or relabel unavailable actions, let users select a method, and bind confirmation to the intended target/revision.
acceptance: For a read-only viewer there is no enabled Merge. A conflicting PR displays the blocker. A squash-only repository offers the correct method and the operation reports its actual result.
